Russia released overhead footage of a Geran-5 drone striking a Kyiv business center on September 25, filmed in real-time by a second drone orbiting ~3 km away as a relay/camera platform. 
The strike hit the Incom building (housing Datagroup infrastructure), killing four. 
The filming drone — either a jet-powered Shahed or smaller Gerbera UAV — then left Kyiv and struck a McDonald's logistics warehouse in Brovary. 
This was a coordinated two-drone operation: one strikes, the other provides live battle damage assessment.

events.text:
🔥🔍 Five arrested after explosives found near RAF Fairford — bomb plot foiled 'by chance,' not intelligence
Counter-terrorism police have arrested 5 men after explosives were found on 3 vans parked minutes from RAF Fairford, the US airbase used for bomber missions against Iran.
According to the Guardian, a member of the public spotted unusual late-night behavior and called 999. Police only moved on the vans after that call. The operation was not intelligence-led — investigators had no prior knowledge of the plot.
📌 Fairford has a 3km runway reinforced for B-1 and B-52 heavy bombers — the same aircraft used in strikes on Iran.
In July, Iran's IRGC noted RAF Fairford's use by US bombers, warning the UK that "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces."
Counter-terror police are investigating whether Iran was behind the plot, though nothing is being ruled out. Meanwhile, the UK threat level remains at severe — meaning an attack is highly likely.

events.text:
📑 Netanyahu orders ICC case prepared against Erdogan
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered an interministerial team and legal officials to prepare a case against Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the International Criminal Court, according to i24NEWS.
The case would target Turkey's treatment of its Kurdish population, and allegations that Erdogan's government has financed Hamas.
Neither Israel nor Turkey is a party to the Rome Statute — neither recognizes the ICC's jurisdiction. Sources say Israel hopes to use the proceedings as leverage against Erdogan rather than necessarily filing.
The ICC has issued arrest warrants for Israeli officials over the war in Gaza. The man ordering this case would be arrested on sight in most of Europe. And he's now trying to file paperwork at the court that wants him in a cell.
The ICC has been repeatedly accused of devolving into a[ corruption-steeped political weapon](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/49077), doling out "justice" on a pay-to-play basis, selectively targeting nations who champion multipolarity—those forging independent paths with Russia, China, or others outside Western orbits.
So it may just oblige — serving the very men it issued warrants for.
